textbookText: Class 2: Osteichthyes (Gr; osteon-bone; ichthys-fish) i. They are found inhabiting in freshwater, marine water and brackish water. ii. They have chiefly bony endoskeleton and hence called as bony fishes. iii. Tail is homocercal. iv. Freshwater bony fishes have swim bladder connected with alimentary canal which helps in floating or buoyancy. v. Their mouth is terminal or sub terminal in position. vi. Scales are ganoid, cycloid, or ctenoid and few are naked. vii. They respire through 4 pairs of gills supported by bony arches, covered by operculum. Some of them have air bladder and lung for respiration. viii. Fertilization is external, male has no copulatory organ. ix. Mostly oviparous.
Example: Labeo (rahu), Cyprinus (carp), Cirrhinus (naini), Hippocampus (Sea horse), Exocoetus (flying fish), Anguilla (eel) etc.

Super class 2: Tetrapoda (Gr; tetra-four; podos-foot) Tetrapoda includes animals having two pair of limbs arising from the trunk. They are mostly terrestrial and some of them exhibit amphibious mode of life. Super class tetrapoda consist of following classes:
1. Amphibia (Gr; amphi-dual; bios-life) i. They spend dual mode of life i.e. living in land and water both. ii. Their body is mainly divisible into head and trunk. Some of them have neck and tail.

iii. They have two pair of pentadactylous or five toed limbs. Some of them are without limbs. iv. Skin is soft moist, glandular and with chromatophore (pigmented cells). v. Exoskeleton is entirely absent but endoskeleton is bony with dicondylic skull. vi. Alimentary canal is complete; mouth is wide and bounded by jaws. Tongue is often protrusible. vii. They respire through skin or lung or lining of buccal cavity. In some forms external gills in larva persist in adults. viii. They have three chambered heart with an additional chamber; sinus venosus. Presence of renal portal system and hepatic portal system. ix. Kidneys are mesonephros and excretion is urecotelic in adults. x. Brain is poorly developed with 10 pairs of cranial nerves. xi. Nasal chambers, single ear ossicle (columella) and lateral line system as sensory organs. xii. Sexes are separate. xiii. Fertilization is external, male without copulatory organs. Female are oviparous and egg are laid in water which hatch out into larva which is completely aquatic and respire through external gills.

Unique features Need water for reproduction, locomotion by limbs, body without hard exoskeleton, respire through lungs, skin and buccal cavity, heart 3-chamberd, kidney mesonephric, poikilothermic, cranial nerves 10 pairs, external fertilization, indirect development Example: Rana tigrina (frog), Bufo (toad), Triton (newts), Salamandra (salamander), Siren (mud eel), Hyla (tree frog), Rhacophorous (flying frog), Ichthyopis etc.

Class 2: Reptilia (L; repere-to crawl) i. They are predominantly land dwellers, crawling and some are burrowing forms. ii. Body is bilaterally symmetrical and divisible into head, neck, trunk and tail. iii. Skin is dry without any glands and is covered by exoskeleton such as horny epidermal scales, shields and scutes. iv. They have two pair of lateral limbs arising from trunk which are pentadactyle and digits are with horny claws. Snake and some lizards are without limbs. v. Mouth is terminal in position and jaws are with simple conical teeth. vi. Endoskeleton is bony and skull is monocondylic. vii. Presence of 3-chambered heart with the exception in crocodile (4-chambered). RBCs are oval and nucleated. viii. Lungs are the respiratory organs. ix. They have metanephric kidney and excretion is urecotelic.
